headline: 18-Year-Old Bronx Native Sponsors Ghana Schoolchildren Through Nonprofit
meta_description: Max Owobu, 18, founded the Yenko Foundation to sponsor children's education in Ghana after witnessing kids forced to work instead of attending school.
summary_short: An 18-year-old from the Bronx saw classmates in Ghana working instead of learning, so he started a nonprofit. Now ten children attend school because of him.
body:
At 18, Max Owobu from the Bronx is balancing senior year with running an international nonprofit that has already changed the lives of ten children in Ghana. After witnessing kids his own age working in shops and on streets instead of attending school during summers spent in his father's birth country, Owobu founded the Yenko Foundation at age 15 with money from his allowance. The organization now sponsors children's kindergarten through fifth-grade education, covering tuition, meals, uniforms, and transportation—items that cost families in Ghana what they cannot afford, unlike America's public school system. At just $1,000 per child annually, the foundation has enabled a full decade of young students to access quality education at Calvary Methodist, a school Owobu chose after witnessing the genuine joy students displayed there.

The foundation's work addresses a real challenge in Accra: while private schools often provide better education than public alternatives, the market is rife with operators who charge parents hundreds of dollars for minimal instruction. Owobu's careful vetting process—guided by a local contact—helped him avoid these pitfalls and establish a sustainable model centered on one school and genuine need.

With ambitions to expand his impact before graduation, Owobu plans to sponsor between ten and fifteen children through primary school completion, then extend the foundation's reach to hospitals and orphanages across Ghana. His story is a reminder that meaningful change doesn't require waiting for adulthood—or a trust fund. It requires attention, intention, and the willingness to act on what breaks your heart.
quick_facts: Max Owobu, 18, founded Yenko Foundation while in high school
Foundation sponsors ten children's K-5 education in Ghana
$1,000 covers tuition, meals, uniforms, and transport for one year
Students attend Calvary Methodist school in Accra, Ghana
Max plans to expand to fifteen sponsored children before college
